summary: Well-executed, fully artifacted preregistered paired study that implemented a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The run and analysis are reproducible and transparently reported; the observed result was a degenerate null (all 200 shared initial candidates were validator‑valid, so no repairs occurred). The manuscript correctly documents the preregistration, execution artifacts, and the interpretive limits arising from the shared_initial_candidate design, but it requires a small set of manuscript clarifications and bibliography fixes before finalisation.
critical_issues: Title and some high‑level phrasing risk implying the paper measured the full, end‑to‑end effect of GVR on independently sampled generations; the executed estimand (validator/repair effect on a single reused sampled candidate per intent) is narrower and must be stated consistently in title/abstract/introduction/conclusion and any contribution claims.

References metadata/format: several cited_record_ids are identifier‑only (DOI/arXiv/URLs). The manuscript must present a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata for each cited work and ensure each numbered citation in text supports the proximate scholarly claim.
required_revisions: Explicitly and prominently make the estimand/design constraint unavoidable in the paper title or subtitle (or the first paragraph of the Introduction) so a reader cannot interpret the experiment as having measured independent per‑condition sampling or prompt‑engineering effects; state verbatim that baseline and guarded reused one sampled candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate) and therefore the experiment tests post‑generation deterministic validation/repair only.

Replace identifier‑only reference entries with a conventional IEEE numbered References section containing full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/URL where appropriate). Ensure every inline numeric citation (e.g., [1]) maps to a full IEEE entry and that each cited record supports the specific claim for which it is referenced.

In Results and/or Methods, add an explicit, concise statement that the McNemar test (and associated inference) is uninformative in the observed degenerate case of zero discordant pairs, and clarify that the reported p=1.0 and CI=[0.0,0.0] reflect that degeneracy rather than evidence of equivalence.

Ensure any remaining in‑text DOI/arXiv/identifier mentions are replaced by numeric IEEE citation markers; do not leave raw DOI or arXiv URLs in running text or reference list when full metadata is available.
optional_revisions: Consider changing the title to explicitly indicate the study evaluated the downstream validator/repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics (e.g., append a short parenthetical).

Add one short sentence in Methods pointing to the archived model_configuration.json path and hash (already in the evidence bundle) to help readers locate sampling metadata, while keeping Disclosure concise.

Briefly expand Discussion with a concrete recommended follow‑up preregistered design (e.g., independent per‑condition sampling, adversarial task subset) and quantify how that design would change planned model call counts and estimand interpretation.
